raw_case_text:
A 38-year-old male, diagnosed as HIV-positive, presented to our department with multiple painful, erythematous skin lesions over extremities, face and abdomen of 2 days duration along with the history of evening rise of temperature with chills, malaise, body pains, joint pains, and ankle edema. The patient had history of nasal stuffiness and epistaxis. He was not a known case of leprosy. He was on ART zidovudine, lamivudine, nevirapine (ZLN) for 4 weeks prior to the onset of skin lesions. Further, history of sexual exposure with multiple heterosexual partners was noted. No history of diabetes mellitus, hypertension, or tuberculosis.
On general examination, he was pale, thin built, ill nourished and febrile. On examination, there was no generalized lymphadenopathy. There was diffuse infiltration of ear lobe [Figure 1]. Multiple erythematous, tender papules, and nodules were present on the face [Figure 2] and also on trunk and extremities [Figure 3]. Sensations of pain and touch were reduced over both the feet. Ulnar, radial cutaneous, lateral popliteal, and posterior tibial nerves on both sides were thickened and tender. Hair, nails and mucous membranes were normal. Systemic Examination revealed no abnormalities.
Hematological Examination revealed microcytic hypochromic anemia (Hb: 10 g%), and neutrophilic leukocytosis (TLC: 12,800/mm3) differential count N75L20M3E2, and raised ESR (68 mm in-first hour). VDRL was non-reactive, and HBsAg was negative. The findings of complete urine examination were normal. Blood glucose levels, renal function and liver function tests were normal. Chest X-ray and ultrasonography of abdomen were normal. HIV-1 was reactive, the viral load was 1,07,400 copies/mL and CD4 count 94 cells/cu. mm before starting ART. At the time of diagnosis of IRIS, which is 1 month after starting of ART, CD4 count was 151 cells/cu. mm. Slit skin smear examination for M. leprae revealed bacteriological index of 4 along with a morphological index of 20%. Biopsy taken from the nodule on the left hand [Figure 3] demonstrated mild hyperkeratosis in epidermis, grenz zone. Dermis shows edema with collection of macrophages [Figure 4]. Vessels showed acute and chronic perivascular inflammatory infiltrate [Figure 5] consistent with ENL.
On the basis of the history, clinical examination, and investigative findings, a diagnosis of IRIS presenting as ENL in a patient of HIV with unmasking of lepromatous leprosy was made.
The patient was continued on ART and started on MBMDT (rifampicin:-600 mg, dapsone:- 100 mg, and clofazamine:-50 mg). He was given oral steroids which were gradually tapered over a period of 3 months. After 9 months of MBMDT and ART, no further episodes of ENL were reported and his CD4 count is 367. The patient is doing fine and attending to his duties.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old HIV-positive male on antiretroviral therapy for 4 weeks presented with a 2-day history of multiple painful erythematous skin nodules over his face, abdomen, and extremities accompanied by evening fevers with chills, malaise, myalgias, arthralgias, and ankle edema.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Four weeks after initiating combination antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine, lamivudine, and nevirapine), the patient acutely developed multiple tender erythematous papules and nodules over his face, trunk, and extremities over 2 days, accompanied by evening fevers with chills, generalized body and joint pains, bilateral pedal edema, and a prior history of nasal stuffiness and epistaxis.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV-1 infection diagnosed prior to starting zidovudine/lamivudine/nevirapine (ZLN) 4 weeks earlier (baseline CD4+ count 94 cells/mm3, viral load 107,400 copies/mL). No prior known history of leprosy, tuberculosis, diabetes mellitus, or hypertension. Sexual history notable for multiple heterosexual partners.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for painful skin nodules, evening fever with chills, malaise, myalgia, arthralgia, ankle edema, nasal stuffiness, and epistaxis. Home medications: zidovudine, lamivudine, and nevirapine.

objective.physical_examination: Pale, thin, ill-nourished, and febrile without generalized lymphadenopathy. Cutaneous and neurological examination revealed diffuse bilateral earlobe infiltration, multiple tender erythematous papules and nodules across the face, trunk, and extremities, reduced pain and light-touch sensation over both feet, and bilaterally thickened and tender ulnar, radial cutaneous, common peroneal (lateral popliteal), and posterior tibial nerves. Hair, nails, mucous membranes, and systemic exam were normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed microcytic hypochromic anemia (hemoglobin 10 g/dL), neutrophilic leukocytosis (WBC 12,800/mm3; 75% neutrophils, 20% lymphocytes, 3% monocytes, 2% eosinophils), elevated ESR (68 mm/1st hour), nonreactive VDRL, negative HBsAg, and normal urinalysis, blood glucose, renal, and liver function tests. Chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound were normal. Slit-skin smear for Mycobacterium leprae was strongly positive with a bacteriological index (BI) of 4+ and a morphological index (MI) of 20%.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count at IRIS presentation (4 weeks post-ART) had risen to 151 cells/mm3 (from 94 cells/mm3 at baseline, and reaching 367 cells/mm3 at 9 months). Punch biopsy of a left hand nodule demonstrated mild epidermal hyperkeratosis, a subepidermal Grenz zone, dermal edema with foamy macrophage collections, and acute-on-chronic perivascular leukocytoclastic inflammatory infiltrate diagnostic of erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Unmasking immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) presenting as erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL / Type 2 lepra reaction) and lepromatous leprosy 4 weeks after initiating zidovudine/lamivudine/nevirapine in a 38-year-old male with HIV-1 infection (baseline HIV-1 viral load 107,400 copies/mL, CD4+ count rising from 94 to 151 cells/mm3; confirmed by slit-skin smear BI 4+ / MI 20% and skin biopsy histopathology). The patient was continued on ART, initiated on WHO multibacillary multidrug therapy (MB-MDT: rifampicin 600 mg, dapsone 100 mg, and clofazimine 50 mg), and treated with a 3-month tapering course of oral corticosteroids. At 9-month follow-up, he remained completely free of recurrent ENL episodes with a CD4+ count of 367 cells/mm3.
